title: LSP-DETR: Efficient and scalable nuclei segmentation in whole-slide images

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《LSP-DETR: Efficient and scalable nuclei segmentation in whole-slide images》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and objective · abstract-1-1】Precise and scalable instance segmentation of cell nuclei is a fundamental prerequisite for computational pathology, yet gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) pose significant computational challenges. While patch-based processing is standard during training, existing methods are often limited to small tile sizes during inference due to architectural bottlenecks or reliance on computationally expensive post-processing steps for instance separation. We introduce a faster, scalable, and end-to-end framework capable of processing large-scale image tiles while accurately modeling biologically realistic overlapping nuclei.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《LSP-DETR: Efficient and scalable nuclei segmentation in whole-slide images》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We propose LSP-DETR (Local Star Polygon DEtection TRansformer). The model represents nuclei as star-convex polygons and employs a lightweight transformer with linear complexity, enabling the processing of high-resolution images in a single forward pass. A novel radial distance loss accommodates annotation uncertainty, allowing the segmentation of overlapping nuclei to emerge naturally without explicit overlap labels.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《LSP-DETR: Efficient and scalable nuclei segmentation in whole-slide images》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】LSP-DETR achieves state-of-the-art efficiency, with an inference time of 0.45 s/mm2 representing a 3.2× speedup over StarDist, the next-fastest method. On PanNuke, the model achieves competitive accuracy (67.5 bPQ), while yielding an F1-score of 0.964 in polygon overlap when evaluated against consensus annotations from two expert pathologists. Furthermore, it outperforms larger models such as LKCell in terms of generalization robustness, reaching an F1-score of 85.0 on MoNuSeg.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】LSP-DETR bridges the gap between high-fidelity segmentation and practical clinical requirements by eliminating heuristic post-processing. By providing a scalable, linear-complexity solution that naturally handles overlaps between nuclei, this framework sets a new direction for efficient high-throughput WSI analysis in digital pathology.
